messages:
oncall-bot: :rotating_light: PAGER: P0 - Increased 95th latency and 503s from hosted API (region: us-west1). Impacting text-generation endpoints. Pager sent to eng-oncall primary. Link: https://incidents.redwood.ai/1893456789
Alex: saw the alert, jumping in. first look: spike started ~1893456700, 503 rate ~6% overall, 12% for certain model routes. affected: hosted API only — dedicated pools look fine from metrics.
Maria: cc @infra_oncall @sec_oncall — can infra confirm networking / infra-layer throttles? adding support to customer-notify list.
Jim: quick question — do we route all backend 5xx to infra or runtime? this originated from runtime autoscaler errors last time.
Sara: from our last incident doc, runtime should be primary for model-serving errors (KV cache, OOM, batching). infra if we see networking, kube node drains, or LB issues. security only if we see auth anomalies or malicious traffic patterns.
Alex: good call. I see increased TCP retries on the model-serving nodes in us-west1. stacktrace from runtime logs shows repeated 'Failed to allocate KV cache' warnings. Posting snippet: ```
2026-03-14T21:06:12Z runtime[worker-3]: WARN Failed to allocate kv_cache: OOM, free=120MB required=512MB
2026-03-14T21:06:13Z runtime[worker-3]: ERROR request handler: 503 service_unavailable
```
infra_oncall: I'm here. looks like node memory pressure — but need full node-level metrics. pulling node-exporter and kube events. If nodes are under memory pressure, we'll check eviction thresholds and recent deploys.
sec_oncall: no signals of auth spikes or strange traffic from WAF. not security so far.
support_lead: can someone confirm customer impact so I can draft a banner? which customers affected (hosted API users only or dedicated too)?
Maria: dedicated customers unaffected per logs. impact estimate: ~8% of requests degraded or 503 in us-west1; global traffic partially routed to other regions but latency increased for region-bound requests. list of high-traffic API keys attached in our internal dashboard (link masked).
Alex: mitigation plan proposal: 1) drain affected worker pods gracefully to allow KV cache warmup fallback 2) increase runtime pod memory limit temporarily for canary 3) if that fails, fallback route policy to model-variant-quantized to reduce memory pressure. 4) alert infra to look at node-level pressure and evict/expand nodes.
Jim: +1 to warming fallback. pinging infra to do node resize if needed. infra_oncall: I'll scale node pool by +2 in us-west1 now. watch for kube-scheduler backpressure.
infra_oncall: kicked off a +2 node scale, ETA ~120s to register. also seeing one daemonset crashloop that may be leaking memory. investigating.
Alex: assigning owners: runtime primary = @alex, runtime secondary = @maria. infra primary = @infra_oncall, infra secondary = @jim. security = @sec_oncall on standby. support contact = @support_lead.
Sara: note for handoff later: my shift ends 23:00 UTC. there's a coverage gap 00:00-01:00 UTC where we don't have a secondary assigned for runtime — can someone cover that window? :thinking_face:
maria: I can extend to 00:30 UTC but then I have a hard stop. who can cover 00:30-01:00?
jim: I can pick up 00:30-01:30 if needed, but prefer if we avoid heavy ops then.
support_lead: I'll prepare a short external status: "experiencing partial degraded performance in us-west1 for hosted API; mitigation underway — we will update in 30 minutes." draft ready for review.
Alex: operational notes and runbook pointers: follow Runbook: "runtime-kv-cache-oom" https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/runtime-kv-cache-oom and infra runbook: "node-memory-pressure" https://docs.redwood.ai/runbooks/node-memory-pressure. Key steps pasted: ```
- Check worker pod memory usage (kubectl top pod -n runtime)
- If allocation errors, increase pod memory limit by +1Gi for canary
- Drain & restart pod with grace to repopulate KV cache
- If node pressure, scale node pool or cordon+drain the node with highest memory usage
- If suspect leak, collect pprof and open an ops ticket to eng-runtime-team
```
Maria: also adding a temporary routing change: add fallback route to model-variant-quantized for high-TTL requests. I can apply the route 2min.
infra_oncall: node scale complete, new nodes ready, kube autoscaler caught up. memory pressure dropping. I'm still going to investigate the daemonset leak and post a ticket.
Alex: after scaling, 503 rate dropped to ~1.2% and p95 latency trending down. keeping monitor for 15m.
onchalant-bot: :white_check_mark: Auto-monitoring check — 503 rate now below threshold.
Sara: thanks all. small admin/handoff: I'll update the oncall calendar and note that runtime primary@alex covers until 23:00 UTC, runtime secondary@maria extends to 00:30 UTC, runtime backup@jim 00:30-01:30. infra stays on rotation with @infra_oncall primary.
Jim: for cross-team routing clarity: please use these rules going forward — runtime-team handles model-serving errors, infra handles node/cluster/LB, security handles auth/WAF anomalies, support handles customer-facing comms. if unclear, ping #eng-oncall and tag both runtime and infra.
support_lead: customer banner posted. will update with next status in 30m.
Alex: wrapping up for now: monitoring window started. if anything spikes again, escalate to paging policy level 2. otherwise I'll prepare a post-incident note with timeline and remediation steps. :thumbsup:
